newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: FOCUS-Avonmore Waterford merger jobs fears.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Avonmore Waterford merger jobs fears.

text.p: Ireland's food producer Avonmore Foods Plc formalised its offer for rival Waterford Foods on Monday but failed to quell fears of jobs cuts voiced by employees and farmers.

If the merger goes ahead the new group will generate a combined turnover of 2.5 billion Irish pounds ($3.9 billion) and 71.5 million pre-tax profits and will catapult the food company onto the world stage with interests on both sides of the Atlantic.
Analysts say the merged entity, to be called Avonmore Waterford, is an excellent fit, creating many synergies which analysts expect will generate substantial economies of scale and cost cutting.
"They are a superb fit. There are tremendous cross synergies in their operations," Goodbody analyst Liam Igoe said after the initial announcement.
Igoe said both companies have an almost identical range of businesses including the manufacture of butter, cheese and liquid milk and both are in agri-trading such as animal feeds and fertilisers.
But it is for this reason that employees and farmers fear for their jobs with some media reports estimating up to 800 jobs may be on the line due to rationalisation.
"The feeling here is one of concern," senior Amalgamated Transport and General Workers Union (ATGWU) official Tony Mansfield told Reuters.

"There is a throw-way remark in the middle of all this analyst speak on the merger saying they see up to 20 million Irish pounds cost savings due to rationalisation of overlapping processing facilities. That obviously means closing down areas," he said.
Mansfield said this was most likely where the extra 3.25 pence per gallon offered by Avonmore to farmers, if the offer is successful, comes from.
He said such a gain was a "a false ecomony" as far as people working there are concerned because of what it may cost them in terms of jobs.

Mansfield said his trade union, which represents the majority of Waterford's workforce will meet with other unions during the week to discuss the planned merger. Avonmore said this was not a hostile bid when it formalised its offer on Monday offering one Avonmore share for every two Waterford Foods Plc and Waterford Co-op Ltd ordinary shares.
Waterford Foods and Waterford Co-op said in a separate statement on Monday that they were studying the proposal and would respond in due course.
To succeed the merger must be ratified by 75 percent of Waterford Co-op (who own 68 percent of the Plc shares) and Waterford Foods Plc members.
Avonmore argues that further consolidation is needed in the Irish dairy industry and that the deal would be in the best interests of shareholders and milk suppliers for both organisations.
It warned that the food sector is facing enormous change and challenge which could have very adverse effects on the income and livelihoods of farmer members for both organisations.
Waterford's share price was holding at 100 Irish pence by mid-morning Monday up from a pre-announcement price of 80 pence. Avonmore's share price hit 237 Irish pence up from a close of 228 on Friday.
